result.question: How did Mahatma Gandhi transform Indian nationalism into a mass movement between 1915 and 1931? Discuss. (Answer in 250 words)

directives.meaning: Look at the issue from more than one side, with reasons, and reach a balanced view.

sentences.text: When Gandhiji returned from South Africa in January 1915, Indian nationalism was largely confined to the educated elite.
Within fifteen years he had turned it into a movement of peasants, workers and women.
Satyagraha: In South Africa he had already forged satyagraha, his technique of non-violent protest.
At the opening of the Banaras Hindu University in February 1916, he charged the Indian elite with neglecting the labouring poor.
Struggles in Champaran (1917), Ahmedabad and Kheda (1918) showed his sympathy for the poor.
Rowlatt Satyagraha: His countrywide campaign of 1919 against the Rowlatt Act made him a national leader.
Public anger deepened after Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to fire on a meeting at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar.
Non-cooperation: He joined hands with the Khilafat Movement of the Ali brothers, which demanded that the Turkish Sultan, as Khalifa, retain control over Muslim holy places.
Students left government schools, lawyers boycotted courts, and peasants and tribals interpreted the call in their own ways.
He withdrew the movement after the violence at Chauri Chaura in 1922.
Organisation and symbols: Provincial Congress committees were organised on linguistic lines, while the charkha, khadi and the campaign against untouchability made him a Mahatma to the poor.
Salt Satyagraha: After the Lahore Congress adopted Purna Swaraj in December 1929, he began the Dandi March from Sabarmati on 12 March 1930 and broke the salt law.
Women took part in large numbers for the first time in a nationalist campaign.
The movement led to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931 and his presence at the Second Round Table Conference.
By uniting moral appeal with organisation, Gandhiji made nationalism truly mass-based, and his methods still shape democratic protest.
